name: Beach Day Outcomes
description: Rules for picking one outcome per day and rendering the e-ink screen. Evaluate outcomes in array order and stop at the first whose `when` passes; `jacket_day` is the catch-all and must stay last.

location.label: VENICE BEACH
location.note: Shown as the eyebrow on the left panel. Change per install.

precipChanceMaxPct.description: Peak hourly chance of rain during daylight

cloudCoverAvgPct.description: Daylight average, drives the SUNSHINE stat

conditionSummary.description: Short phrase from the weather API, e.g. 'Clear sky'

sunRunHours.description: Length of the longest unbroken run of daylight hours with cloudCover <= 30

sunWindow.description: That run as a compact interval, e.g. '1P-4P'. Empty when nothing is clear.

rainWindow.description: First to last daylight hour with a rain chance over 20%, e.g. '10A-3P', or a single hour when that is all there is. Empty when the day stays under the threshold - show the percentage instead.

evaluation.note: Wet and cold are checked before hot so a cold rainy day can never resolve to a warm-weather outfit. beach_day must be checked before sun_hat_day: they share the hot-and-sunny base, and only wind, air quality and cloud cover separate them.

DAY
outcomes.note: Catch-all: anything cool, grey or unremarkable that isn't wet, freezing, hot or swingy.
outcomes.alsoGrab: Also grab: a hoodie for the ride home — it cools off fast.

sections.headline: {outcome.title joined by line break}
sections.statStrip: {stats} — five columns: icon, label, value, word
sections.footerNote: Plain text under the stat strip. Tokens: {sunsetLocal}, {footerSuffix}. The outcome's footerSuffix is only used if the template asks for it — e.g. "Sunset: {sunsetLocal} — {footerSuffix}". A filled black bar is reserved for the parking warning, so it still means 'act on this'.

heroColor.note: Colour panels only (reTerminal E1002). One flat ink across the hero panel, which is a third of the screen - the verdict is readable from across a room before a word is. Available inks: yellow, blue, red, green; 'none' leaves it black or white. Deliberately used on only the three days that demand a decision, so each colour stays learnable: yellow means go to the beach, blue means take rain gear, red means it is genuinely cold. Everything else is neutral, which is also what keeps the palette from turning into confetti. Type colour is chosen automatically - black on yellow, white on the darker inks. A mono panel ignores this entirely and uses heroPanel, so the black-and-white design is unchanged.

heroPanel.note: Per-outcome, on the outcome itself. 'dark' is white type on a black panel; 'light' is black type on white. Reserve 'light' for the days worth looking up for — a bright panel reads as good news, and on the 6-colour display it lets the hero icon show its real inks.

rules: Never phrase a stat as a question and never show a checkmark — the value plus its plain word carries the verdict.
Exactly four wear tiles per outcome so the grid never reflows.
Every outcome except beach_day is named after a garment.
Copy stays readable by a first-grader: short words, one idea per line.

design.rendering: 1-bit e-ink, no greyscale dithering in type
